subject: DPA redline: on-demand erasure, backup exceptions & legal-hold flow
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Lee <hannah.lee@datasecure.com>, contracts@datasecure.com
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 Jan 2027 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: DPA redline: deletion & backup exceptions — follow-up

Hannah / DataSecure contracts team,

Thanks for sending over your annotated DPA. Attached is a clean redline (redline_dpa_v3.pdf) and our operational erasure playbook (erasure_playbook.md) to give you more context on how deletion and backups work in practice on Redwood. High-level summary of the current proposal from our side: 

- Primary customer data (active indexes / request logs / model inputs) — eligible for deletion on request; standard turn-around: we schedule the erase and mark the object tombstoned within 24 hours, and full removal from primary stores completes within 60 days in our standard offering.
- Backups & archived snapshots — retained for disaster recovery; standard retention is up to 12 months and is encrypted at rest. Backups are not typically included in on-demand erasure unless the customer signs a Backup Purge SLA.
- Certified deletion attestation — we can provide a signed attestation/certificate for the deletion event and a low-level audit of the activities. Typical delivery window we support today: 10 business days from completion of the purge.
- Regional residency — we can run a Private deployment (EU-only) or Hosted with EU-only tenancy. If you require on-prem snapshots or physically onshore-only backups, that's supported as an add-on and will change the ops model.
- Legal hold / subpoena — we will follow legal hold exceptions: we do not proactively delete data if required by an order, but we will limit retained material to the minimum required and notify the customer.

Could you confirm whether DataSecure needs: 1) a 30-day primary deletion window, 2) backup retention capped at 90 days, and 3) certified deletion within 5 business days? Those are the most aggressive asks we see and will require an internal DR/legal review to confirm feasibility and risk.

Proposed next step: 30-minute call (Friday 16th or Monday 19th) to walk the redline and any carve-outs you want for backups / forensic retention.

Thanks,

--
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
pri...@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132

Priyom,

Appreciate the materials — they help. Short responses: DataSecure is firm on three asks for the DPA:

- Primary deletion window must be 30 calendar days from request.
- Backups must not exceed 90 days retention (we can accept a short legal-hold carve-out).
- Certified deletion attestation must be issued within 5 business days after deletion completes.

We require EU-only residency for all production copies (including routine snapshots).

Also need clarification on immutable backups vs. recoverable snapshots — our security team needs guarantees that once we ask for purge, backups will not be used for restore unless we explicitly opt-in. Attached is our preferred redline (datasecure_redline.docx). If you cannot accept this exact language, please propose a compromise that includes tight SLAs and auditability.

Thanks,

Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 08:32:00 +0000
Subject: Re: DPA redline: deletion & backup exceptions — follow-up

Hannah — thanks for the clarity and the redlines. I discussed with the ops and legal teams this morning. 

Operationally + risk summary from Redwood:

- 30-day wipe for primary data is aggressive for our standard hosted/dedicated offering because of delta replication, delayed compaction, and retention in encrypted backups. We can offer a compromise: 45 calendar days for primary deletion. During that window we will tombstone objects immediately and prevent any new reads; background compaction + index rebuilds complete within the window.
- Backups: to meet recoverability SLAs we cannot accept a 90-day hard cap for all customers by default. We can offer a policy: default backup retention 180 days but include a Backup Purge SLA that allows you to request a targeted purge of snapshots that contain your data (subject to verification) within 60 days from request for a fee. For EU-only customers on Private deployment, we can tighten that to 90 days.
- Certified deletion attestation: we can commit to providing a signed attestation within 7 business days after the completion of the purge for standard customers; for Private / on-prem accounts we can target 5 business days.
- Immutable backups: we can add contractual language that backups will not be used as a source for restore of your account without explicit written consent from DataSecure.

I've attached an updated redline (redline_response_v1.pdf) that contains the proposed compromise language and a suggested Backup Purge SLA section. Can Laura and Irene confirm whether the compromise above is acceptable legally, and whether we should add explicit escrow/forensic attestations in the DPA?

If this looks broadly acceptable, propose a call on Wednesday 20th at 10:00 CET to finalize.

Best,
--
Priyom Das
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redline_response_v1.pdf (PDF, 28 KB)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 Jan 2027 11:18:00 +0000
Subject: RE: DPA redline: deletion & backup exceptions — legal guidance

Team,

Quick legal take on the proposed compromise:

1) Primary deletion window: 45 days is a reasonable commercial compromise. We should be explicit that tombstoning occurs immediately and that "completion" means removal from primary stores and indexes; however, we must carve out a narrow exception for legal hold and for data that is required to be preserved for compliance with regulations. Include language: "Except to the extent required by applicable law or valid legal process, and subject to the minimal retention necessary to comply with such obligations."

2) Backups: offering 180 days by default with an option to tighten to 90 days for EU Private deployments is acceptable. We should add a Backup Purge SLA appendix that: a) defines the verification process for identifying snapshots that include the customer's data; b) lists a fee schedule / operational lead time (we should avoid open-ended promises to purge encrypted backups without adequate verification); and c) requires the customer to acknowledge potential residual metadata retention for billing/operational reasons.

3) Certified deletion attestation: 7 business days for hosted is reasonable; 5 for Private is aggressive but attainable. The attestation should be scoped (what is included — object identifiers, timestamps, hashes, scope statement) and should not be open-ended.

4) Immutable backup language: good to include explicit "no-restore" without written consent. Also include a clause for forensic requests from law enforcement that requires Redwood to notify the customer where permitted.

5) Escrow & forensic: propose an appendix for escrowed keys/forensic snapshot access for a fee (useful for enterprise customers).

I will draft redline snippets for the DPA and the Backup Purge SLA appendix and circulate by EOD.

-Irene
Irene Choi
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Data Protection
Redwood Inference

Hannah — thanks again for the frank feedback and for the redline. Following legal and ops review (Irene and Laura looped in), here's a concrete compromise we can put into the DPA and the Backup Purge SLA appendix: 

- Residency: Redwood will provision an EU-only Private control plane for DataSecure (no cross-border replication) for production.
- Primary data erasure: 45 calendar days from request; immediate tombstone at request time and prevention of reads; "completion" defined as removal from primary stores and indexes.
- Backups: default retention 180 days for hosted; DataSecure's account on Private deployment will have default 90 days. We will include Backup Purge SLA: targeted purge requests for identified snapshots will be processed within 60 calendar days for hosted (30 calendar days for Private) after verification.
- Certified deletion attestation: 7 business days for hosted; 5 business days for Private. Attestation will include object IDs, timestamps, and a scope statement.
- Legal hold: Redwood will not purge data subject to a valid legal hold; Redwood will notify DataSecure of any request to retain or provide access where permitted by law and will limit retained material to the minimum necessary.

Next steps: Irene will send DPA snippets and the Backup Purge SLA appendix (EOD today). If this is acceptable, let's schedule a 30 min call to confirm and then we can issue an updated DocuSign packet. Proposed time: Wed 27 Jan, 11:00 CET. HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/HS-482917.

If you want the Private control plane priced out before we proceed to DocuSign I can loop in solutions engineering.

Best regards,
--
